newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish shares on highs, led by Ericsson/property.
newsitem.headline: Swedish shares on highs, led by Ericsson/property.

text.p: Sweden's bourse climbed to a new high on Tuesday after reversing early losses, with telecoms giant Ericsson and the property sector leading.
The Stockholm general index, which has risen eight out of the past nine days, gained 0.97 percent to close at 2,140.61 after shares worth 3.8 billion crowns changed hands.
"It was a little hesistant at the open, but it then showed that the bourse continues to be strong," a broker said.
"Right now it seems it could go further."
Ericsson was a focus of the market after U.S. rival Motorola posted its third quarter results overnight Monday.
The stock rose 4.50 crowns to 175, its highest level since September last year when it hit a record 186 crowns.
Market players were mixed on their opinions for the rise.
"Yesterday's Motorola report has certainly given some support," an analyst told Reuters.
The property sector saw large gains, rising 6.31 percent. Skanska jumped 19.50 crowns to 286.50 but brokers were unable to pinpoint any specific reason for the jump.
Newly listed Diligentia was the day's third most traded stock and it closed 5.50 crowns higher at 90 crowns.
